note: The measurements ByteMe offers. One shared list: the website (app.js) and the Python scripts (build_world.py, tests) both read it. 'code' is the NASA POWER parameter name. 'scale' multiplies the raw value (soil wetness 0-1 becomes percent). 'percent' says whether a percent change makes sense (zero means 'none of it'). Search: 'phrases' (several words, strong match) and 'keywords' (single words) link a question to a measurement. Avoid very general words such as water, air or ground: they appear in questions about many measurements. 'not_available' lists things people ask for that this data set does not have, with what to say and the closest measurement we do have. Measurements with "dataset": "nasa" come from data/nasa/ (built by build_nasa_grids.py); 'pair' names the NASA POWER measurement they double-check.

variables.name: Air temperature
variables.definition: How warm the air is 2 metres above the ground, averaged over day and night.
variables.keywords: temperature temperatures hot hotter warm warmer warmed warming warmth cold colder cooling heat climate degrees
variables.phrases: air temperature, near-ground air, near-surface air, 2-m air, 2 m air, two metres, above the ground, warmth of the air, near surface temperature, air-temperature, near-surface air

variables.name: Hottest temperature of the month
variables.definition: The highest air temperature reached during each month.
variables.phrases: maximum temperature, daily maximum, hottest days, hottest temperature, days above, over forty degrees, above 40

variables.name: Coldest temperature of the month
variables.definition: The lowest air temperature reached during each month.
variables.keywords: minimum coldest frost frosts freeze freezing nights lows
variables.phrases: minimum temperature, coldest nights, coldest temperature

variables.name: Surface temperature
variables.definition: How warm the ground or the sea surface itself is (its 'skin').
variables.phrases: surface temperature, skin temperature, sea surface, sea-surface, ocean surface, at the surface, ground temperature

variables.name: Air temperature (AIRS satellite)
variables.definition: How warm the air is just above the ground, measured from space by the AIRS instrument (average of its day and night passes).
variables.phrases: airs satellite

variables.name: Land surface temperature (MODIS)
variables.definition: How warm the land surface itself is, seen from space by MODIS (average of day and night). Land only.
variables.phrases: land surface temperature, ground temperature from space

variables.name: Rain and snowfall
variables.definition: How much rain and snow fall each day on average.
variables.keywords: rain rains raining rainfall rainy precipitation downpour downpours wet wetter drought droughts monsoon storms
variables.phrases: from the sky, rain or snow, water equivalent, rain and snow

variables.name: Evaporation from land
variables.definition: How much water moves from the ground and plants into the air each day. Land only.
variables.keywords: evaporation evaporate evaporates evaporating evaporated evapotranspiration transpiration
variables.phrases: into the air from, to the air from, back into the air, back to the air, returns to the air, to the atmosphere, into the atmosphere, giving off, gives off, given off, sent back, water loss, loss to the air, lost to the atmosphere, becoming vapor, becoming vapour, releases into the air, going out

variables.name: Relative humidity
variables.definition: How close the air is to holding all the water vapour it can (100% = saturated).
variables.phrases: relative humidity, percentage of the moisture, close to saturation

variables.name: Water vapour in the air
variables.definition: Grams of water vapour in each kilogram of air near the ground.
variables.phrases: water vapour, water vapor, specific humidity, moisture in the air

variables.name: Water in the whole air column
variables.definition: If all the water vapour above you fell as rain at once, how deep the layer would be.
variables.phrases: precipitable water, whole air column, air column, column of air

variables.name: Rainfall (GPM satellites)
variables.definition: How much rain and snow fall each day on average, measured by the GPM satellite constellation.
variables.phrases: gpm imerg, satellite rainfall

variables.name: Evaporation (GLDAS)
variables.definition: How much water moves from the ground and plants into the air each day, from NASA's GLDAS land model. Land only.

variables.name: Runoff (GLDAS)
variables.definition: Water that drains off the land into streams and rivers, over the surface and underground, from NASA's GLDAS land model. Land only.
variables.phrases: overland flow, runs downhill, runs off, water draining

variables.name: Surface soil wetness
variables.definition: How wet the top 5 cm of soil is: 0% is completely dry, 100% is fully soaked.
variables.phrases: top layer, topsoil, top centimetre, top centimeter, top 1 cm, top 5 cm, surface soil, surface-only soil, skin of dirt, thin skin, upper soil

variables.name: Root-zone soil wetness
variables.definition: How wet the soil is where plant roots grow (top metre): 0% dry, 100% soaked. Land only.
variables.keywords: soil moisture roots root rooting dirt crops crop farming farmland agriculture dry drier drying
variables.phrases: root zone, root-zone, rooting layer, root layer, where plants root, where plant roots, crop roots, for plants, plant-accessible, soil moisture, soil water, water in the soil, moisture in the soil, water stored, water held, water retained, left in the ground, water storage, rooting-layer

variables.name: Snow depth
variables.definition: How deep the snow lying on the ground is. Land only.
variables.phrases: snow depth, snow on the ground, layer of snow, snow cover, snowpack thickness

variables.name: Root-zone soil moisture (GLDAS)
variables.definition: How much water the soil holds where plant roots grow, in kilograms per square metre (= millimetres of water), from NASA's GLDAS land model. Land only.

variables.name: Vegetation greenness (MODIS)
variables.definition: How green and leafy the land looks from space (NDVI): near 0 is bare ground, above 0.6 is dense green vegetation. Land only.
variables.phrases: less green, more green, vegetation greenness, plant growth
variables.keywords: greenness green greener vegetation ndvi leafy forest forests deforestation crops

variables.name: Wind speed
variables.definition: How fast the air moves 10 metres above the ground.
variables.keywords: wind winds windy windier breeze breezy gust gusts
variables.phrases: wind speed

variables.name: Air pressure
variables.definition: The weight of the air above pressing on the surface.
variables.phrases: air pressure, surface pressure

variables.name: Ozone layer
variables.definition: The total amount of ozone above you, in Dobson units. Ozone high up shields life from UV light.
variables.phrases: ozone layer, ozone hole

variables.name: Haze and dust in the air
variables.definition: How much tiny particles (dust, smoke, pollution) dim the sunlight. 0 is perfectly clear air; above 0.4 is hazy.
variables.keywords: aerosol aerosols haze hazy dust dusty smoke smoky smog pollution polluted particles particulate wildfire wildfires
variables.phrases: air quality, dirty air, haze and dust

variables.name: Nitrogen dioxide (OMI)
variables.definition: How much nitrogen dioxide (NO₂, a gas mostly from traffic, power plants and fires) is in the lower air, measured from space by OMI. Higher means more polluted.
variables.phrases: nitrogen dioxide, air pollution, traffic pollution
variables.keywords: no2 nitrogen dioxide traffic exhaust emissions

variables.name: Sunlight reaching the ground
variables.definition: The energy of the sunlight that arrives at the surface each day, clouds included.
variables.keywords: sun sunny sunnier sunlight sunshine solar brightness dimming
variables.phrases: solar radiation, solar energy, sunlight reaching

variables.name: Cloud cover
variables.definition: The share of the sky covered by clouds.
variables.keywords: cloud clouds cloudy cloudier cloudiness overcast
variables.phrases: cloud cover
